#1348. What Man United, with their seemingly addictive habit, must do now once Michael Carrick is sacked: IAN LADYMAN on Sir Jim Ratcliffe's trail of bad judgment and waste

Published: 02:00 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 07:53 EST, 10 November 2026

Those who were there will never forget the utter chaos of Michael Carrick’s last act at Old Trafford. But as the outgoing United manager clung on to his dignity like a life raft in those mad closing moments against Aston Villa, the current poster boy for United’s desperate demise sat on the bench in his tracksuit.

Diogo Dalot is an honest and by all accounts fully committed Portuguese full-back who has been a United player for more than eight years.

The 27-year-old was bought for his teenage potential by his compatriot Jose Mourinho in 2018 but has never trained on. He has never been good enough for a really top English club yet has made more than 250 appearances for the most famous one of all and has played for five different permanent managers.

On Sunday he was booed off by his own supporters when substituted after an hour. His had been a particularly grim performance but the boos were not about him, not really.

No they were not about Dalot but instead about the fundamental truth of what he represents. Namely a steady, grisly and unforgivable drain of footballing standards at United that actually began in the final days of Sir Alex Ferguson and has subsequently never stopped.

It is this that has taken United from Ferguson’s final valedictory title of 2013 to where they are today, the bottom three of the Premier League. It is this that has drained United of all their clout and reputation. It is this that has cost yet another United manager – a seventh – his job.

Diogo Dalot has become the poster boy for the decline under Michael Carrick as Man United seemingly plumb new depths

The outgoing club legend is not a good enough manager for United and his appointment was yet another mis-step by the club's hierarchy

Carrick is not a good enough manager for United. His appointment was an emotional mistake, one of many made by Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the band of misfits and hopefuls who are currently in charge of football operations.

With a better manager – a better coach – in charge of the current team, United would be in the top half of the league. The fact they sit 18th and resemble a Sunday League team that never gets going until they have shaken their hangovers off is squarely down to him.

Nevertheless, United are a football club that exists to win trophies, no matter what the majority owners the Glazers may have said recently. But United will not win the big trophies again until they buy better players and by that I mean better footballers and better people.

It sounds simple, trite even. But it’s a simple truth of our game. Until United can reverse a seemingly addictive habit of paying too much money for too little, the difference made by a manager will only ever be a matter of six or seven places in the Premier League standings. And United needs a much greater improvement than that until this vicious cycle of self-harm comes to an end.

There is so much wrong at the modern Manchester United away from the field. Much of it begins and ends with the hideous hubris and self-regard of Ratcliffe, a man so shot through with misplaced self-confidence that he still insists on being tailed everywhere by a journalist he has hired to write a book on United’s journey back to the top of the mountain. Suffice to say that one won’t be ready for this Christmas.

But the thread that links the final days of Ferguson and his chief executive David Gill through the years of Ed Woodward, Richard Arnold and John Murtough to these dark days of Ratcliffe’s INEOS control is simple. It’s sub-standard players.

Despite the financial drain of the Glazers’ stranglehold, United have spent in the region of £1.75bn on their first team in the last ten years.

It takes quite something to do that and take a club backwards. It takes quite something to do that and buy only one player – captain Bruno Fernandes – who can claim to have been consistently effective over his time at the club.

Somehow, though, United have managed it and it is this hideous trail of bad judgment and waste that follows the current team and those that have come before it every time it runs out on to the field.

United are weak off the pitch and even weaker on it. Their football mirrors their off-field strategy. Haphazard, wasteful and inconsistent.

A number of years ago – at a time when previous CEOs Woodward and Arnold were trying to mend a broken club - they enlisted the advice of Ferguson, Sir Bobby Charlton and former captain Bryan Robson to help them work out what exactly a United team should be.

‘Exciting, daring, confident and humble’ were the key words they laid down. Well, what on earth happened to any of that?

United have a huge decision to make – yet again – over a new manager. The field of suitable candidates is not as big as they would like. Nor is United as attractive a proposition as it was. The demands are enormous yet the foundations shake. It’s not a good combination.

A good coach would improve them. Carrick has had two central defenders on his staff in Jonny Evans and Jonathan Woodgate. What on earth have they been doing for the last two or three months?

Long before the arrival of Jim Ratcliffe former chief executive Ed Woodward and Richard Arnold attempted to draw a blueprint for the club

Their successors in the boardroom Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox have not impressed over a baffling summer

But United remain four or five good transfer windows away from where they need to be and the last time they put a run of good business like that together at Old Trafford Carrick was probably in the first team.

United need proper talent but they also need proper people, not the kind who would rather moan to TV cameras after a defeat than go home and think about their own part in what has just happened.

Last summer’s strategy seemed to have come straight out of Chat GPT and reflects terribly on the current football director Jason Wilcox. To ‘fix’ the midfield through three signings with the need to ‘fix’ the back four kicked down the road for 12 months is not so much a strategy as an exercise in transfer suicide.

Some think Wilcox should follow Carrick through the door on the back of that and it’s a reasonable point of view. Viewed through the mist of an autumn afternoon on Sunday, Wilcox looked as grey as his recent track record. An alternative take is that the recruitment of players like Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha is indicative of an uptick in returns, at least in part.

Whichever path you wish to walk, it simply has to lead to an improvement in the one area that will either nourish or starve a football club. With that in mind, the first question a prospective manager should ask is who is buying the players and on the back of what long-term strategy.

Carrick’s United team have looked like exactly what they are this season, a group put together by different people following different principles for different managers. How strange that it hasn’t worked.

United, as we know, needed a left-back over the summer. Lewis Hall, of England and Newcastle, may have been an option. Instead, United placed their faith in Luke Shaw, a 31-year-old with a long history of injuries.

Shaw, unsurprisingly, is currently injured which brings us back to where we started, namely the sight of the right-footed Dalot labouring out of position on the left of Carrick’s back four against Villa on Sunday.

You could say we saw this coming. Many did. In the dressing room and in the stands at Old Trafford. Carrick? He knew about it, too, but then he was only the manager.

His exit will hurt for a while. He is an emotionally intelligent and empathetic individual who will reel from the trauma of the last ten weeks. Over time he will realise that he is well out if it, though. When he took the job last summer, Ferguson is known to have been concerned about what it may do to him. As often, Carrick’s old boss was right.

United are set up to fail and Carrick’s replacement will realise that soon enough. When he walks into the first team dressing room for the first time and looks for those upon whom he can rely to consistently help him, too many eyes will be focussed on the floor.

#1346. Everton Women Welcome JYSK As Official Home Furnishing Retail Partner

Everton Women has announced a new partnership with international home furnishing retailer JYSK, which will become the Club's ‘Official Home Furnishing Retail Partner’.

The agreement brings together Everton and the Danish retailer, renowned for its Scandinavian-inspired furniture and homeware, in a partnership that will enhance facilities at Goodison Park and support community initiatives across Merseyside.

JYSK (pronounced 'YOOSK') operates more than 3,600 stores worldwide, with a presence in the Liverpool City Region through its outlets in Hunts Cross and St Helens. The Scandinavian retailer will provide furniture and homeware to create welcoming spaces for players, staff and supporters at Goodison Park.

The announcement marks Everton Women's third dedicated commercial partnership, following agreements with GGM Gastro and, most recently, Nestlé Confectionery, further demonstrating the growing appeal of the Club to leading international businesses.

Everton Women's move to Goodison Park has provided a distinctive platform for commercial growth, combining the Club's rich footballing heritage with new opportunities for partners to play a meaningful role in the future of women's football.

JYSK will also support the work of Everton in the Community, with furniture featured in the partnership's launch campaign donated to the charity's 'Home Is Where The Heart Is' programme, which supports young adults experiencing or at risk of homelessness.

The donated items will make a valuable contribution to the charity's four-bedroom residential property in the L4 area of Liverpool, further enhancing the welcoming and supportive environment provided for young people as they develop the skills and confidence needed to live independently.

Andrew Middleton, President of Business Operations at Everton, said: "We're delighted to welcome JYSK to Everton Women. There's a natural connection between a business that helps people make a house a home and the next chapter we're creating at Goodison Park, and we're looking forward to bringing that to life for our players and supporters.

"What particularly stands out is JYSK's commitment to making a positive difference beyond football. Their support for Everton in the Community is a fantastic example of how we want our partnerships to deliver meaningful benefits, both for the Club and the communities we represent.

"There's a growing recognition among businesses of the opportunities around Everton Women, and we're focused on building partnerships that go beyond traditional sponsorship. JYSK is another great addition to that journey and we're excited about what we can achieve together."

Roni Tuominen, Country Director, JYSK Ireland & UK, said: "Everton Women has an incredible story with a rich heritage and community roots. The team has made a positive start to the season and we can’t wait to support them at Goodison Park and help turn this legacy stadium into a home."

JYSK's partnership will be visible at Goodison Park for the first time when Everton Women host Durham Women in the Subway Players Cup on Wednesday 11 November (7pm GMT kick-off), with branding featuring on the stadium's big screens and pitchside LED advertising.

To celebrate the announcement, JYSK will also give away limited-edition JYSK x Everton tote bags at its Hunts Cross Retail Park store on Saturday 14 and Sunday 15 November.

The bags will be available to customers making a purchase, with no minimum spend, on a first-come, first-served basis while stocks last.

For more information about JYSK, visit jysk.co.uk.

Villa’s set-piece coach, Pal Fjall, is a former Viking assistant coach.

If Aston Villa beat Viking tonight, they'll be the second fastest team to reach 20 European Cup/UEFA Champions League victories (in their 30th game), only behind Real Madrid (won 20 of first 29). After a summer of upheaval, Unai Emery has got his Villa team clicking once again. In this form, they'll be confident of securing another win. @DavidSegar_ looks at how Emery's turned their poor early-season form around ahead of tonight's clash. 🔗 https://t.co/wV6Mr6vLio

There is already a lot of noise from the 2,000 or so Viking FK supporters in the away end.

Last week the club marked their return to the Champions League by securing a famous 3-3 draw with heavyweights Bayern Munich. Viking had led 2-0 at half-time before rescuing a point in the last minute.

A first win of the campaign tonight would represent another huge shock.

Villa’s co-owner Nassef Sawiris is in the house tonight.

Sawiris was the main driver behind the appointment of Unai Emery almost four years ago. Worked out ok, hasn’t it?

Elsewhere in Europe this evening, Manchester United are currently 4-0 down against Cesc Fabregas’ Como. Nico Paz has starred with two goals and an assist. Could this spell the end of Michael Carrick’s tenure in charge of Man Utd? You can keep up with the action and post-match reaction here.

Speaking to the club’s official website in his match preview, the Aston Villa boss said: “Champions League, every team they are playing Champions League, they are because they deserve it and they are dangerous and they have their collective and individual issues or characteristics as a team.

“Viking, they drew against Bayern Munich last week, they lost against Stuttgart. They are with Bodø/Glimt in the league, first and second with the same points.

“Bodø/Glimt is a team successful the last years in Europe, performing well, getting good results, playing Champions League, beating important teams.

“So Viking now is a new team as well, with the with the capacity to draw against Bayern Munich, the capacity as well to compete against Stuttgart and to compete against us tomorrow.

“This is Champions League, and Champions League is very difficult. In Champions League, we have now six points, it’s something amazing, but very difficult, and to keep the same way we are is our challenge.

“It’s not only Champions League, because Europa League is very difficult, and Conference League is very difficult. Europe is always very difficult.

“This is the first respect. We are Champions League, and each team is, of course, very, very respectful for us.”

Ibrahim Mbaye has slowly been embedded into the first team picture at Aston Villa by Unai Emery following his big money to England in the summer. The 18-year-old was used off the bench against Newcastle and looked very likely with his blistering pace and trickery. Mbaye starts this evening and we will be keeping eye on him, given his star quality and talent.

What a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Aston Villa fairytale under Unai Emery was in danger of ending.

With six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, Villa were stepping into the unknown despite the arrival of ten new players.

We have all learned, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

Villa 2.0 have made a flawless start to their Champions League campaign so far and are running into fine form in the Premier League after a sticky start.

This could be another magical season under their brilliant Basque manager, with an exciting and vibrant new team.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Champions League fixture as Aston Villa host Viking in the Midlands.

Villa made history in their previous home Champions League outing last week, thrashing Fenerbahce 6-0 to seal the club’s biggest-ever European win. This emphatic victory, coupled with the hard-fought 3-2 triumph over Club Brugge at the start of September, means that Unai Emery’s side have made a 100% winning start to the league phase. The well-deserved 1-0 Premier League victory over Newcastle United at St James’ Park on Saturday evening has amplified the positivity, with Emery’s new-look squad beginning to meaningfully gel and now boast a five-match unbeaten streak across all competitions.

Prepared for another night on Europe's biggest stage ✨ https://t.co/oZYiIiGvRg

Despite their Viking’s lack of European pedigree, Villa should be wary of their Norwegian opponents, who secured an unforgettable 3-3 draw with Bayern Munich in Stavanger last time out in the Champions League. The hosts initially flew into a two-goal lead at the break, before a double from Harry Kane and a strike from Luiz Diaz hauled the Bavarians ahead. However, after Michael Olise was sent off, Herman Haugen’s 90th-minute headed equaliser rescued a thrilling draw to give Viking their European point this season following a 3-1 loss to Stuttgart on MD1. Domestically, the reigning champions of Norway are joint top of the Eliteserien with Bodo/Glimt and embroiled in a nailbiting title race with just seven games remaining.

Villa’s injury list includes Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Johan Manzambi, who both picked up issues against Newcastle, as well as Amadou Onana and Matteo Ruggeri. Still, the hosts possess more than enough quality to dismantle Viking, particularly with Nicolas Jackson, who has been in effective form recently and netted a brilliant brace against Fenerbahce.

We’ll bring you the latest updates and drama. Kick-off is at 20:00, with team news coming shortly.

#1342. Mauricio Pochettino's 'kill' team talk - when USA were already 3-0 up - convinces Man United fans he's right to replace Michael Carrick

Published: 09:23 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 09:57 EST, 10 November 2026

Excitement is already building among Man United fans at the prospect of Mauricio Pochettino taking charge, if Michael Carrick is sacked.

Carrick is taking training at Carrington today and his future is set to be decided on Wednesday when chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox meet with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco.

If United choose to axe Carrick as expected, with the club in the relegation zone, USA boss Pochettino is the bookies' favourite to take the reins at Old Trafford and footage of a passionate team-talk has convinced some supporters that he would be the right appointment.

A fly-on-the-wall documentary series called Behind The Crest offered insight into the 54-year-old Argentine's management style and recorded his half-time rallying cry, with the USA 3-0 up in a game against Jamaica during the CONCACAF Nations League semi-finals in 2024.

Pochettino is seen building himself up into a frenzy, telling his players: 'Every single ball is the most important ball. We cannot play like we are winning 3-0.

'We need to go there and show the mentality. Take the next 45 minutes seriously. Take it like it is 0-0 and we need to win the game. That is the only way we're going to improve in our mentality.

🚨📹 WATCH: Mauricio Pochettino’s half-time team talk with his side already leading 3-0 after the first half!🗣️ “No, we don’t concede. We CANNOT concede. We need to go there and KILL and PLAY.”THAT MENTALITY! 👀🔥#MUFC pic.twitter.com/aXuiZn20i3

Mauricio Pochettino's passionate half-time speech to USA players (above) has convinced some Man United fans he would be the right man to take charge is Michael Carrick is sacked

'Be respectful with ourselves, first we need to respect ourselves. We cannot just go there and say to ourselves, "okay 3-0, no problem, they concede, we concede". We cannot concede! We have to go there and kill!

'If you are tired, we have players on the bench who can make a clear, clear impact and desperate to play. We have to press all together. When you're tired you can say, "coach, I can do no more".

'Enjoy being serious, we need to score the fourth, fifth, the sixth. That is the way we grow and respect the opponent.'

Despite the rousing speech, the USA went on to lose the second half but came out on top 4-2 in the match.

The footage has been widely shared on social media in conjunction with Pochettino's links to the Man United job and plenty of fans endorsed the idea of recruiting him, perhaps longing for a manager who can fire up the players in the mold of Sir Alex Ferguson's infamous hairdryer treatment.

One wrote: 'That intensity is what i want to see at United, 3-0 up at half and still no letting off.'

Another posted: 'He is right man for this moment!'. But others were more skeptical, with one capturing the sentiment of other naysayers, writing: 'Even if you hype him he is still gonna fail... if the same board keep of making decisions.'

Pochettino's work with the USA national side earned more plaudits at the World Cup on home soil, where they played excellent football before being dumped out by Belgium in the last-16.

And another of Pochettino's half-time speeches was viewed as a crucial turning point for his tenure in the USA.

With the team drawing 1-1 against Australia in 2025, Pochettino ranted: 'That is football! If we want to compete and we are 1-1 because we have the quality, we need to show more quality in the next 45 minutes. Play together. If you make a mistake, I don't care, but communicate and fight. They [Australia] come and they fight. When are we going to fix that? The team is dead. You need to talk!'

It was the first time Pochettino lost his rag and raised his voice at players since taking charge and midfielder Sebastian Berhalter said the message of the speech was: '"We're American. We don't take s***." Even though he's Argentinian, he has that mindset of, "Look, this is what we do. This is who we are. This is what America's about." Even from an outside perspective, he showed us Americans what we're about. He really drills that into us.'

The USA won the game 2-1 and the manager later reflected: 'This speech helped and was a great opportunity for the coach to explain to the players what to expect on the pitch. It was a tough conversation, but I think it was necessary.'

Perhaps that tough love is what Man United's dressing room now needs.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport late on Monday night, Carrick is nearing the sack during this November international break after presiding over a horrendous start to the campaign with the club in 18th and been given a stay of execution.

It’s understood that the Old Trafford hierarchy would want to inform Carrick of their decision face to face, so there may not be any confirmation from the club until Thursday.

Pochettino, pictured managing Southampton against Sir Alex Ferguson's Man United in 2014, could bring the intensity fans have missed since their legendary manager departed

The 45-year-old turned up for work at Carrington at 7.15am on Tuesday to oversee training with the players who are not away on international duty amid increasing uncertainty over his future.

United sources maintain that a final decision has yet to be made, with the club reluctant to engage in a running commentary over Carrick's position.

Former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino has a £7million release clause in his USA contract. However, it is yet to be determined the true value of prising Pochettino out as that figure doesn't include buying out his backroom staff.

It is also believed within Pochettino's deal that there is another clause which would allow him to leave his US role for particular high-profile jobs, such as at Old Trafford.

As of Tuesday morning, Betfair have him at 4/7 with out of work trio Eddie Howe (5/2), Julian Nagelsmann (5/1) and Didier Deschamps (15/2) the next favourites.

#1341. Harry Kane proves there is only one Ballon d’Or winner

Let’s cut to the chase. If there is any justice, sanity or logic in football then Harry Kane will win the Ballon d’Or when the ceremony takes place in London on Monday.

Arsenal would have deservedly won this Champions League match away to Bayern Munich if Kane was not on the pitch. Instead, they almost lost it but for another bit of brilliance from Declan Rice, Kane’s vice-captain for England, and probably his successor to wear the armband.

A brilliantly worked team-goal finished off by Declan Rice, and Arsenal are level 💥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/Y25zI80A0z

“I’m lucky I can play with him and not so lucky I have to play against him,” Rice said, and that summed it up succinctly.

And that Ballon d’Or? There is bias, but Rice – who is also on the 30-strong list of nominees – added of Kane: “He is the clear winner. His numbers speak for themselves, the year he has had has been remarkable. When you play with him you realise how good he is and when you play against him you see how much of a pain it is.”

Arsenal stood toe-to-toe with Bayern in an open match. Both sides went for it, partly because they knew under the Champions League format, that defeat was not a disaster. There has been some chat about whether Arsenal can be, well, a bit dull. Not here. It would be no surprise to see these two face off again deep into this competition.

The only setback for Arsenal was a worrying injury to Bukayo Saka early on, limping off and tapping his thigh, indicating an issue with his muscle. Mikel Arteta’s reaction betrayed his understandable concern.

Kane won a penalty and then expertly took it to give Bayern the lead. Other strikers could have scored the penalty but few would have created the wonderful assist that drew Bayern level.

It has been a fact for quite some years that Kane is not only the best goalscorer for England but the best passer. Indeed, if Kane could provide for Kane he would have scored even more goals.

“Unsere nummer neun,” shouted the stadium announcer after Kane’s goal and that needed no translation. Kane is a god in Bavaria, where they know a few things about having great centre-forwards. But the 33-year-old is surpassing them all.

Kane’s goal meant he had scored in 10 straight Champions League games, one short of the record held by Cristiano Ronaldo. It was also the former Tottenham Hotspur forward’s 16th goal in 23 games against Arsenal. No one has ever scored more against them.

Kane is the complete player, carrying out his defensive duties – winning headers to clear Bayern’s lines from Arsenal free-kicks – to linking the play to being the focus of his team’s attacks. He is a centre-half, central midfielder and centre-forward. Who pops up on the wing to deliver pinpoint crosses.

Maybe Kane will be pipped at the Palladium – the theatre where the ceremony takes place – by Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal or Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé, or even an absurd sympathy vote for Lionel Messi. But Kane deserves it. His time is now.

Some passages of play in the first half deserve analysis. Just to highlight how good Kane was. After an Arsenal corner, wastefully volleyed over by Riccardo Calafiori, Bayern countered and suddenly it was three on two. Serge Gnabry, the former Arsenal winger, had to do better than shoot weakly when picked out on the overlap. David Raya saved. That was a let-off.

But who sprung that counter? It was not Manuel Neuer, the Bayern goalkeeper, taking the goal-kick, but Kane, with his sharp thinking. And then Kane launched a superb pass from deep which Ismael Saibari should have dealt with better. It should have been another opportunity. Potentially a goal.

Is there anything Harry Kane can't do? 🧐 His goal kick very nearly led to a Bayern Munich goal 😲 https://t.co/fqbsN7KOjw

And then Bayern did score. The ball was played inside to Kane, in centre field and afforded too much space. He delivered a perfectly weighted through ball for Alphonse Davies to run on to. The pace was perfect, allowing the Canadian not to break stride and stroke it past Raya. Kane did not fire the ball in, he did not make Davies work to reach it and he did not give Jurrien Timber any chance of cutting it out. It was perfect. Few players could do that. “Harry Kane puts the ball in a space from 30 metres that doesn’t exist,” Arteta said. True.

Harry Kane with an OUTRAGEOUS assist, and Alphonso Davies equalises 🥵 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/6cGXrUloHW

It was Saka’s replacement who gave Arsenal the lead, Eberechi Eze profiting from Martin Odegaard’s perceptive, lofted pass and taking advantage of Bayern’s ragged defending and some suspect goalkeeping from 40-year-old Neuer to score from an angle. Initially it was ruled out for offside, but that was overturned after a VAR check to provide Eze with a bit of redemption after being hooked against Nottingham Forest at the weekend.

VAR has given it, and Eze strikes Arsenal into the lead at the Allianz 🔥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/i1LjrZVnbI

Neuer had his own slice of redemption as he saved well from Bruno Guimarães’ close-range header, pushing it against a post with Raya also excelling to beat out another header, this time from Dayot Upamecano.

When Timber was punished for handball, as he blocked Kane’s shot, the penalty was given. Up stepped Kane and we knew the rest. At that point it felt like Bayern would win, but Arsenal continued to play courageously and pushed on, as they had done throughout, risking conceding further goals.

Harry Kane, what a penalty 🥶 He scores in his TENTH consecutive Champions League game to give Bayern the lead 😳 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/4k4jPCQEWF

They were rewarded as Rice started the move, playing the ball in quickly to Noni Madueke with substitute Viktor Gyokeres laying it back into the midfielder’s path. He strode on and Neuer was again beaten from an angle. It was certainly warranted, even if it did not detract from Kane’s night. But will he have a greater one on Monday?

It had similarities [with last year’s league phase game]. I think we managed to create more chances but I think that Arsenal – and it’s something that has been mentioned by them before the game – they’ve worked a lot on retaining the ball and making it difficult to get the ball back. We did feel that.

It was a game in chunks. They had moments, we had moments. In our moments, I think we exploited the spaces in behind a little bit better maybe but we played against a top team and the result is a result between two big teams.

Last year they reaped the benefits of a top-two finish: home ties all the way to the final and a guarantee of avoiding the other club in the top two.

They have a chance to pick off Real Madrid at the Emirates, and will anticipate Aston Villa (who still have to play Barcelona and PSG) and Real Betis dropping points.

Given PSG have already dispatched Manchester City and Barcelona, it is hard to envisage them dropping a point, though they do have the odd off night.

Arsenal’s chances of grabbing second could come down to winning their remaining games and Liverpool slipping up. But with five games to go, these permutations are probably premature.

Wow, what a game. That is one of the highest levels that we have played. The level of opposition, what the game required, and our level as well. Two teams who wanted to press each other and wanted to attack and wanted to play. It was a fascinating game.

I think we started the game incredibly well, we were so dominant, we did everything to deserve the first goal. We didn’t score the goal and lost Bukayo and had to adapt to it.

We gave a terrible chance away after our corner which could have cost us, then we scored the goal. In the second half, the game was even,  they started probably a little bit better before they scored and they you have to react and we certainly did.

The spirit of the team, the quality we have showed on the second goal as well.

They are a bit concerned. A player having to come off with a sharp pain is never good news but we have to wait and see.

For me he’s the clear winner, his numbers speak for themselves. He’s obviously up against some other world class players. When you play with him you see how good it is, and when you play against him you see how much of a pain he is! As a striker to play that pass for the goal... he’s ridiculous. Lucky I can play with him, not so lucky when I have to play against him.

I thought it was a good performance. Probably the draw was a fair result overall. We probably just didn’t get quite enough right tonight to get the win.

Nice to get the assist to get back into the game and then I thought we had some good moments but not enough over the 90 minutes.

When you play against teams like Bayern who are man to man all over the pitch you have to apply certain principles, and I just kept running and managed to get away from my man. When they are following you all over, I just kept running and I was in on the goal.

He’s been making such a good impact from the bench [Gyokeres]. He’s made some great runs tonight and set me up for the goal. When you play against man to man, who follow you everywhere over the whole pitch, it’s such a tough game. You have to apply certain principles and concepts, and you’re constantly thinking about where the space is. For the goal, Noni one-touch set, Viktor’s one-touch set, those little movements put you through on goal.

In periods of the game, it felt like Arsenal were trying to play in the manner of Bayern or PSG by leaving themselves so light at the back with acres of green grass to cover.

Would they play like that in a quarter-final? Probably not, and they were emboldened by Bayern missing some key players. But it helped them create danger and have some strong spells, even if there were some scary moments going the other way.

Somewhere between that display and Arsenal’s rearguard in the Champions League final is probably the sweet spot.

A high-quality game between two of the most plausible winners of this season’s Champions League finishes level.

It was a helter-skelter contest at times. For all the talk of Arteta being a conservative coach, Arsenal committed numbers forward in their press and when they attacked, and that left them vulnerable to Bayern’s fast transitions and Kane’s passes from deep.

Perhaps it is a missed opportunity to beat Bayern in the Allianz, given the German side started without Olise, Kimmich, Musiala and Diaz, but a point from the hardest fixture of the league phase is more than acceptable.

The fly in the ointment is the injury suffered by Saka in the first half, but Eze and Madueke performed well in his absence.

Just one minute to play and Bayern have the ball in Arsenal’s half, but Calafiori gets his foot in. Madueke does well to keep it and Lewis-Skelly finds Eze.

Timber with dig from outside the box after a poor defensive header from Bayern, and Neuer tips it over. Rice to take the corner, and Arsenal’s set-pieces have caused problems throughout. This might just be Arsenal’s chance to win it.

Swung to the back post, but Tah did enough.

Bayern had an injury worry of their own now: Luis Diaz, not judged fit to start, has pulled up and will have to come off. Bayern were in a promising position in the Arsenal half.

Harry Kane looking for another of those arced passes forward, but Eze read it and retrieved. Arsenal finishing the stronger when it comes to possession and territory. Perhaps that Premier League intensity bearing fruit as the game progresses.

A couple of fouls given away by both teams, it has been a bitty few minutes. But Arsenal do well to find Lewis-Skelly free in the middle of the pitch, and he finds Rice who drives the away team forward.

Neither team appears inclined to settle for the draw, but Arsenal have the wind in their sails. Mikel Merino is on for Martin Odegaard, who has probably been Arsenal’s best player on the night.

Arsenal back level again, and it is an emphatic finish across Neuer from Rice, after a deft touch from Gyokeres around the corner at the edge of the box. Bright football around the box from Arsenal. Still 10 minutes or so to play.

Arsenal have been scoring gorgeous team goals all season. They have done so in all three of their Champions League games this season. They were labelled as “boring” after the Forest victory but that game was the exception, rather than the rule, on the evidence of this campaign.

A brilliantly worked team-goal finished off by Declan Rice, and Arsenal are level 💥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/Y25zI80A0z

Arsenal deep in Bayern territory after Rice’s cross towards Eze glanced off the head of a defender. Bayern are keeping a good defensive shape though, Arsenal finding it difficult to penetrate. Arteta is preparing another pair of changes.

Luis Diaz with a snap shot that brings a sharp save from David Raya. On the balance of chances and threat created, Bayern have earned their lead. But still plenty of football to play. Arsenal have not scored from a set-piece this season, but they have looked dangerous tonight. They need another couple.

Neuer has just smashed into Stanisic, sweeping up a long ball Timber was chasing.

With Tzolis out and Saka now likely to be joining him on the sidelines, at what point does Arteta turn to Dowman in the league and Champions League? Obviously there are so many physical and defensive demands that are very difficult for a 16-year-old to meet... but the talent is there.

Arsenal enjoying plenty of territory and possession now, but you’d say Bayern look more likely to score on the counter-attack. Arsenal content to keep the ball and set themselves for a late assault.

Lewis-Skelly with a no-touch turn in midfield but then he takes too long and Bischof wins the ball cleanly. Davies nutmegs Rice on the counter, but Madueke tracked back diligently to snuff out the danger. At the other end, Karl fouls Eze who has enjoyed a strong game, aside from his goal.

Laimer with a foul on Eze near the left-corner of the penalty area, so Arsenal have a free-kick in a promising position for a cross. Havertz, Konsa, Gabriel and Timber the targets.

Brilliant deliver from Odeegard, somehow Arsenal fail to apply the finishing touch from a few yards out.

Bayern then escape and stream forward on the break, and Laimer snaps a shot wide.

Bayern Munich lead for the first time on the night. Kane with a short stutter, before sending Raya the wrong way and wrapping the shot into the back of the net with power.

Bruno Guimaraes and Odegaard with some silky touches to help Arsenal win a free-kick in midfield. Arteta has some of his subs warming up, though he has already used one with Saka going off early on.

Arsenal respond though, and Arsenal win a corner through Eze.

Tah replaces Kim at centre-back, so a like for like change.

Arteta will be very disappointed by how Bayern were able to find Kane free in the middle from a throw-in. Whether Konsa should have been higher or Madueke further across, it was too simple.

A high-wire act from both teams, who are pushing numbers forward with and without the ball. Lots of man-to-man duels all over the pitch, and when one is lost there is loads of space to exploit. It has made for an entertaining half, and 1-1 is a fair scoreline. Arsenal controlled the first 25 to 30 minutes, but Bayern have looked dangerous.

The bigger story for Arsenal is the thigh injury suffered by Saka. It would be very surprising to see him before the November international break, at best. He pulled up abruptly.

Lovely Bayern move, whenever they reach three or four passes against Arsenal’s man-to-man pressure they have runners flying forward. Gnabry takes on a shot from a tight angle, and it deflects behind for a corner. Raya does well to claim.

Alphonso Davies’ pace is causing Arsenal some problems, and now it is Bayern’s turn to have a corner. Arsenal have lost some of their control of the first 30 minutes, but still look dangerous themselves. Timber is fouled from the corner, Arsenal free-kick.

Odegaard with a poor pass in the middle of the park, but Konsa produced a tremendous block to stop Kane’s left-footed shot across Raya.

Within 10 seconds, Arsenal are at the edge of the Bayern box through Rice and they win a corner after Eze’s shot was blocked.

The corner is flicked to the back post, where Calafiori was inches away from scoring from six inches out. Close to Arsenal’s first set-piece goal of the season.

The game is stretched now and quite entertaining, a very different feel to Arsenal’s Premier League assignments. Konsa realised Arsenal were short of numbers and lunged in against Harry Kane, hacking him down at the expense of a booking. Rice and his team-mates recovered well against the counter in any case.

Kane with another superb pass, perfectly curled around Timber into the path of Alphonso Davies who finishes beyond Raya. Kane had too much space in the middle of the pitch, Madueke perhaps guilty of not narrowing in.

Kane has played some absolutely absurd passes in this first half and that was the best yet. Alphonso Davies is so quick that Arsenal were never going to catch him, and the pass was so good that David Raya could not come to it.

Harry Kane with an OUTRAGEOUS assist, and Alphonso Davies equalises 🥵 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/6cGXrUloHW

A word of warning for Arsenal is that Kompany has Lennart Karl and Luis Diaz sat on his bench. At least one of those attackers will be on at half-time unless something changes.

Arsenal winning most of the aerial battles and duels for second balls at the moment, Bayern not building any pressure or fluency. There has been the odd flash of danger when Kane flips a pass in behind but Arteta’s team are comfortable at the moment.

Odegaard almost finds Eze with a lovely disguised through ball.

There was a 30-second flurry from kick-off where Bayern had Arsenal’s penalty area under siege, but Arsenal have controlled the game well since and they have another corner. Odegaard has enjoyed the extra space on offer all game. Arsenal’s captain whips the corner to the back post where Guimaraes was free, but he shins a volley wide.

That makes two goals in three games for Eze. Although he got hooked at half-time in one of them (against Forest on Sunday). It feels like that’s probably how it’s always going to be with a player like him, to be honest. Highs and lows.

Arsenal had to wait for the VAR intervention, but they have the lead in the Allianz thanks to a high-quality goal. Odegaard released Eze in behind with a lovely ball forward, and the former Palace man steadied himself before drilling a left-footed shot across Neuer.

Good work from Odgegaard in midfield, one lovely flick to help Arsenal restore some control.

Then Eze puts the ball in the net with a fine finish across Neuer but the flag goes up for offside. This will be checked by VAR... Stanisic, the Bayern left-back, was lingering behind his team-mates on the opposite side of the pitch.

Kane’s range of passing in evidence again, with a driven diagonal over Gabriel’s head towards Saibari but he could not control the ball that was fizzed towards him. Kane is drifting towards the left to open up the pitch for those crossfield passes.

Arsenal caught out on the break by Harry Kane taking a goal kick, from which he picked out Davies with a raking pass down the left. Saibari helped the ball on for Gnabry who was free on the right, but Raya was down quickly to save and Rice cleared.

Arsenal have a corner, after a nice Madueke backheel released Timber. They have the upper hand in this game, but they have lost a major attacking reference with Saka going off. It’s a case of Arsenal’s weakest area being weakened further. From the corner, Calafiori stretches out a leg but directs the ball over.

Arsenal enjoying the lion’s share of possession so far, which is perhaps a reflection of Bayern’s absentees. Kane has just dropped into his own box to receive a pass, and Konsa followed him all the way.

Alphonso Davies runs beyond the Arsenal defence for the first time in the game after Gnabry dribbles past Madueke, but Gabriel made a good challenge from the wrong side.

Ezri Konsa just followed Harry Kane all the way into the Bayern penalty area. Kane loves to drop deep and Arsenal have clearly decided to stick on him, no matter where he goes. For a few moments, Kane was the deepest Bayern player and Konsa was the most advanced Arsenal player.

Havertz has been booked for a foul on Stanisic. Bayern have not been able to build a head of steam as an attacking force so far, but their pressing has forced Arsenal into longer balls forward. No serious chance so far.

So it is now Madueke on the right and Eze on the left for Arsenal. A shame for the spectacle that neither Saka nor Olise are on the pitch, and the Arsenal man had started the game quite brightly.

Saka had a quick chat with Arteta before going down the tunnel. He gestured towards his left quad.

Big problem here for Arsenal: Bukayo Saka has collapsed to the turf after playing a pass, and he looks to have pulled a muscle in his thigh. That is surely his race run tonight, and it looks like he could be out for a few months based on how he went down. Eze is coming on.

The Arsenal fans high up in the Allianz Arena are singing Saka's name as he hobbles off the pitch. He looks very, very uncomfortable. Eze is coming on, so Madueke will move to the right.

Saibari with a cheap loss of possession in midfield, allowing Saka to go straight at the heart of the Bayern defence. He feeds Havertz on the right, but from the German’s cross the ball would not quite drop for Timber or Saka in a crowded box. There looks space on offer for Arsenal. Do they have the speed and quality to exploit it?

Arsenal’s first foray into the attacking third comes from a Raya clip to Timber, pushed well on from right-back, and the defender’s header inside to Saka was a clever one. Madueke received the next pass, but his touch was a little heavy.

Kim players a good switch of play to Laimer, but Calafiori and Rice snuff out any danger and Guimaraes does well to win a midfield foul.

Calafiori was super advanced within the first 30 seconds, straight into an attacking midfield zone. Davies is indeed playing as a left-winger for Bayern in front of Stanisic. In the very early exchanges, Bayern are enjoying more of the ball, but the game still to settle into a pattern.

Arsenal get the game under way, playing in their navy away kit.

The rain continues to lash down. Jurgen Klopp, Germany’s manager, is in the stands having a flim-flam with Rafael Benitez, who has dashed to Bavaria from Anfield where he watched Liverpool vs Villarreal last night.

It seems like Vincent Kompany may have taken a leaf out of Thomas Tuchel’s tactical book. When Arsenal came here in 2024, Tuchel deployed two left-backs on that flank (Mazraoui and Guerreiro) after saying in the press conference that Arsenal’s right-sided attackers were the danger. Kompany appears to have done the same here with Davies, usually a left-back, starting as a winger.

We are going to have to play I expect three or four different games at different stages throughout the game, so we need to have everybody ready to adapt throughout.

Kane has already played against Arsenal since leaving Spurs, so some of the vinegar has gone out of that sub-plot but it is still worth noting that he has scored 15 goals in 22 appearances against them. Several of those goals have been penalties, but Kane is so much more than a goalscorer these days, especially at Bayern where at times he appears to have a free role.

A fascinating aspect of tonight’s game is how Konsa and Gabriel decide to deal with him. Will Arsenal commit to a man-to-man press, with the centre-backs following Kane well beyond the halfway line, or preserve a more zonal approach?

Manchester United are now 4-0 down against a Como team managed by Cesc Fabregas. There is still 15 minutes or more to play. You can follow the rest of the game here to see if they can stem the bleeding.

Will the substitutes again make the difference for Arsenal tonight? In each of their last three league victories, they have won because of goals scored by substitutes. This speaks to the quality of Arteta’s squad, obviously, but also to the Arsenal manager’s ability to pick the right players for the right moments. Over the last year or so, this has become a real strength.

Karl had been expected to replace Olise on the right, but Kompany looks to have stiffened up his midfield by starting Pavlovic, Laimer and Bischof. It will be interesting to see how Saibari and Kane dovetail, two stick-on strikers. It is not Bayern’s strongest team, with Luis Diaz also on the bench.

Bayern Munich starting XI: Neuer, Stanisic, Kim Minjae, Upamecano, Davies, Pavlovic, Laimer, Bischof, Gnabry, Saibari, Kane

Subs: UIreich, Urbig, Ito, Tah, Brown, Luis Diaz, Boey, Sapoko Ndiaye, Karl, Binder

There was little doubt that Arteta would view this game as one that suits Jurrien Timber rather than Ben White. Arsenal’s manager has changed tack by starting Calafiori, who was rested for Arsenal’s first two Champions League games, but Bayern at the Allianz is a significant step up in grade. Madueke rewarded for his showing at Forest.

Arsenal XI: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Guimaraes, Odegaard; Saka, Havertz, Madueke

🔵 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🟡 Two changes for tonight's test ✊

Vincent Kompany is in the building. It wasn’t clear whether the Bayern head coach would be able to attend tonight’s game because he’s been battling a nasty virus over the last few days. He did not do the usual pre-match press conference yesterday but clearly feels well enough to be here tonight.

In an extract from Sam Dean’s new book on Arsenal’s resurgence under the Spaniard, he reveals that Mike Ashley was keen to bring Arteta to Newcastle United in 2019.

Sam writes: “Arteta also did not have a coaching staff assembled. It is believed that he tried to bring some key individuals on board, such was his interest in accepting Newcastle’s offer, but that the timing was not right for the people he truly wanted. In the end, much to the frustration of Newcastle and Ashley, he said no.”

Arsenal: The Inside Story of Arsenal’s Rebirth Under Mikel Arteta (Pan Macmillan, RRP £22).

This is a proper heavyweight clash but, sadly for the neutrals watching, Bayern are missing some big players. Michael Olise is suspended, Jamal Musiala is injured and Joshua Kimmich is unavailable following the death of his father.

This should all work in Arsenal’s favour, and Mikel Arteta will be looking for a repeat of the energy and quality that his team showed against Bayern last season. Arsenal won 3-1 at the Emirates in November in a performance of real class. It was arguably their most complete showing of the entire campaign.

Ice cold from Martinelli 🥶 https://t.co/uQEHb4x7eH

Some excellent, if disquieting, detail from Sam Dean in this piece about the mood around Arsenal away from the first-team following the news of 60 planned redundancies. Sam writes that there are expecting to be other experienced and influential figures departing. The timing of cuts invites particular scrutiny, coming after the emotional peak of winning the league, record revenues and Mikel Arteta’s new contract.

After Arsenal were beaten by Bayern Munich in a Champions League quarter-final two years ago, Mikel Arteta bemoaned a lack of “magic moments” in attack.

Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.

Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.

A pair of stodgy performances (in victory) against Leeds United and Nottingham Forest have amplified those questions, though some of Arsenal’s slicker football in the season’s early weeks has been forgotten a little hastily.

They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.

Their chances of matching last season’s eight wins from eight could well hinge on the outcome of tonight’s game, but there are worse times to face Bayern.

Vincent Kompany’s team looks as formidable as ever, having scored 22 goals from six Bundesliga games so far this season. Their rotational approach is hard to track, with runners from deep breaking beyond Harry Kane who wanders into deep midfield positions.

However, they are without Michael Olise (suspension) and Jamal Musiala (injury) while Joshua Kimmich will miss the game on compassionate grounds following the death of his father.

With the exception of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincacpie, Arsenal have a pretty clean bill of health and the strength of their bench was crucial against Leeds, Lille and Forest last week.

For Arteta, there are some interesting selection calls to make. It is anticipated that Jurrien Timber will replace Ben White at right-back, and first-choice left-back Riccardo Calafiori has been rested for the Champions League games so far. Should Arteta continue that policy, Myles Lewis-Skelly will fill the position, which will likely mean a midfield start for Bruno Guimarães or Mikel Merino.

Arsenal’s manager must also decide between Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze on the left, and Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front. Havertz is Arteta’s preference, but he also has to consider a relatively short turnaround before Saturday’s league game against Everton.

The 2026 Nature Spotlight: Neuroscience tables are based on the Nature Index database, covering research articles published between 2021 and 2025.

#1339. Ice-Breakers & Idea Planning For New Junior Fans' Forum Intake

Everton’s 2026/27 Junior Fans’ Forum gathered for the first time during October half-term, with the group brainstorming initial plans and ideas for the campaign.

The youngsters, aged 11-16, met at the Blues’ Royal Liver Building headquarters for ice-breakers and to learn more about what they can expect from their meetings with the Club throughout the season.

For the first time since its inception, the Junior Fans’ Forum includes returning members this season, meaning those who were part of the initiative in 2025/26 were able to share their experiences and answer questions from the new intake.

Junior Fans’ Forum membership will continue to be staggered over two seasons going forward to allow for greater continuity year-to-year, while still creating an annual opportunity for young Evertonians to apply for the group.

The move will also enable the Club’s Fan Engagement team to collaborate with the Junior Fans’ Forum on longer-term projects and ideas aimed at younger supporters.

Last season, the group focused on raising awareness of Everton in the Community among their peers, culminating in the group working with Everton's Culinary Experiences Partner Aramark to create a one-off fundraising doughnut that was sold at the annual EitC fixture against Chelsea in March.

In recognition of their efforts, Forum members were joined by Everton defender Jake O’Brien, midfielder Charly Alcaraz and then-Blues winger Dwight McNeil for a special launch event and taste test at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

This year’s Forum members will continue to meet in school holidays throughout the season. For updates from their meetings, keep an eye on evertonfc.com/Fans!

#1337. What Tom Brady's exit means for Birmingham City: Why NFL legend quit St Andrew's, 'body coach' Alex Guerrero's future role revealed - and impact on Knighthead's ambitious £2bn plans for Premier League push and new stadium

Published: 08:41 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 11:15 EST, 10 November 2026

Tom Brady has quit Birmingham but his influence will continue to be felt around the Championship leaders through one of his closest allies.

The club announced via a social media post late on Monday that the NFL legend’s three-year association with Blues would end.

Titled ‘Tom Brady Departure’, the 62-word statement read: ‘Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the club over the last three years.

'It was truly amazing to have someone with Tom's experience and passion associated with the club, and the club looks forward to continuing to build on that foundation from the training ground to the Birmingham community.’

Yet it can be revealed that the ideas of Brady’s ‘body coach’ Alex Guerrero will continue to inform Blues’ push for Premier League football.

Here Daily Mail Sport looks at the reasons for Brady’s departure – and what the future holds for Blues now he has gone...

Tom Brady (right) has left Birmingham City - though their plans remain ambitious under owners Knighthead and chairman Tom Wagner (left)

Brady brought stardust with him to Birmingham and was the figurehead of a new era at the club - despite attending just four matches since buying into Blues

Brady has not been a visible presence in Birmingham for about two years and attended only four matches after he was unveiled as a ‘minority investor’ in 2023, not long after US investors Knighthead had completed their takeover.

It has proved challenging for Brady to divide his time between Birmingham and his commitments in the US, where he has a £280million contract as Fox Sports main NFL analyst. He has also been part-owner of the Las Vegas Raiders since 2024.

Daily Mail Sport understands, however, that Guerrero’s methods will still be used at Blues – a significant detail given his long-term association with Brady.

Described by Brady as his 'body coach', the pair have worked together for two decades and Brady credits Guerrero with extending his NFL career beyond his 45th birthday. With Guerrero at his side, Brady won four Super Bowls and three MVP (Most Valuable Player) awards.

Birmingham chiefs have been very impressed with Guerrero, who they believe has transformed the club’s approach to fitness and recovery.

Since Guerrero came in with Brady, recovery sessions the day after a game have been mandatory and players have had individual conditioning programmes, including tailored advice on nutrition.

Daily Mail Sport understands the methods of Brady's 'body coach' Alex Guerrero (left) will still be used at Blues

In 2025, skipper Christoph Klarer told Daily Mail Sport: ‘We have so many physios and massage therapists who show you exercises in the gym and treat you before and after training. There will always be a physio available at the training ground if I want to see one. That’s not typical.’

Klarer and fellow defender Phil Neumann have not missed a game through injury as Blues players since joining in 2024 and 2025 respectively.

There have been subtle changes, though. Many of the logos and messages from TBRx – Brady’s performance and fitness company – have disappeared from the walls of the training ground in rural Warwickshire. They will be replaced by branding for the recently-launched ‘Keep Right On’ initiative as well as messages that boss Chris Davies believes are particularly relevant to his squad.

At this stage, certainly not. Knighthead remain determined to push forward their vision for Blues, with the £2billion Sports Quarter project at its heart.

The centrepiece of the Sports Quarter is the Powerhouse – a 62,000-seat stadium development that Blues hope will be one of the best in the country.

Blues may have lost their most famous face but all indications are that Brady’s departure is not a sign of Knighthead scaling back their commitment. The US group still believe Birmingham can become one of England’s most prominent clubs and are hugely excited by their progress this term, with Davies’ men top of the Championship heading into the November international break.

Knighthead still believe Birmingham can become one of England’s most prominent clubs and are hugely excited by their progress this term

Chris Davies’ men are top of the Championship heading into the November international break

It is easy to categorise Brady as a mere figurehead but that would be unfair. The 2025 Amazon Prime docuseries Built In Birmingham: Brady & The Blues was streamed in about 200 countries. There is no doubt that Brady’s presence helped Blues push certain transfer deals over the line, with Brady conducting video calls with targets. Earlier this season, Davies was late for a press conference because he had been on the phone to Brady.

The 49-year-old had a good relationship with the squad, too. He developed a strong rapport with former Blues forward Alfie May and even appeared on a FaceTime call during the wedding of May’s brother.

Equally, it would be unwise to exaggerate Brady’s role. If Blues win promotion this term, it will be a combination of Knighthead’s investment and the work of Davies and his players. By elevating the club’s profile globally, perhaps Brady has already done his job. Now it is time for the class of 2026 to write their own story.

During the early part of Brady’s time at St Andrew’s, the club leaned heavily into their rivalry with Wrexham, who are owned by Hollywood star Ryan Reynolds and his fellow actor Rob McElhenney.

When Blues took on Wrexham in September 2024, their 3-1 win was almost a sideshow. As well as the three famous Americans, David Beckham was also at St Andrew’s. When the clubs met, the US stars traded friendly insults before and after the match, generating a great deal of attention on social media.

David Beckham (right) was among the famous faces to take in a Birmingham game alongside Brady

Knighthead remain determined to push forward their vision for Blues, with the £2billion Sports Quarter project at its heart. The centrepiece is the Powerhouse – a 62,000-seat stadium

There was less of this when Blues won 2-1 at Wrexham earlier this season and perhaps that was no coincidence. There have certainly been those at Blues who feel that, at times, the club bought into the Wrexham rivalry a little too much and that forging their own path might be more fruitful.

There is no suggestion that Brady pushed the links with Wrexham yet if he is no longer associated with Blues, they may decline naturally.

In Brady’s first season, Blues were relegated to League One, with the NFL star admitting the club had tried to change too much, too soon. The appointment of Wayne Rooney was the highest-profile of those errors.

Brady departs with the club as healthy as it has been for some time. Even if he was rarely central to that recovery, he deserves at least some of the credit for it.

#1335. Bournemouth thrash Milan to seal greatest win in club’s history

Eighteen years ago, Bournemouth were minutes away from being liquidated and playing in the fourth tier. On Thursday night, Bournemouth not only welcomed AC Milan in Europe; they did so as favourites, and then pummelled them.

When Amine Adli curled in an 84-minute free-kick with his left foot at the Vitality Stadium, it put the seal on the most extraordinary evening in Bournemouth’s history. On a brutally windy and wet night, Bournemouth trounced AC Milan 3-0.

Amine Adli with a SUPERB free-kick to give Bournemouth a 3-0 lead vs AC Milan 🚀 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/KX5i5oM3TG

Milan could not even point to being down to 10 men for the last hour as mitigation; long before, Bournemouth had treated the Rossoneri with contempt. When Ruben Amorim’s side trudged off, soaked and silenced, they had not mustered a single shot on target.

Few nights have better encapsulated the Premier League’s power. Bournemouth have never finished higher than last season’s sixth in the top flight of English football; AC Milan have won seven European Cups. But the Premier League’s financial clout is such that, each season, the bottom club earns more than the champions of Serie A.

The Premier League’s shared riches, allied to years of astute recruitment and management, have underpinned the Bournemouth’s ascent. Even Andoni Iraola’s departure has not stalled the progress at the Vitality Stadium; Marco Rose has relished the new European adventure.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Europa League tie between Bournemouth and AC Milan at the Vitality Stadium.

Back in 2008, Bournemouth’s prospect of a European meeting with Milan seemed impossible. After entering administration with crippling debts of around £4m, Bournemouth were handed a 10-point deduction and relegated from League One. To make matters worse, a hefty 17-point deduction was given to the club ahead of the 2008-09 League Two season, with relegation to non-league seeming inevitable. However, midway through the campaign, the transformative Eddie Howe was parachuted in as Bournemouth’s saviour, eventually guiding the club to safety.

Fast forward to October 2026 in an extraordinary rise and Bournemouth are competing in their first-ever European campaign in the club’s 127-year existence. They welcome Milan to Dorset, having earned back-to-back victories over Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz to kick off their inaugural Europa League adventure in style.

Now, they host the second most successful side in the European Cup history. In terms of heritage and silverware, these clubs could not be further apart, but on the pitch, it’s incredibly tough to call.

On Sunday, Marco Rose’s Bournemouth picked up their first Premier League win of the season, beating 10-man Sunderland 2-0 at the Vitality thanks to goals from Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson to move out of the relegation zone.

Meanwhile, Ruben Amorim is in charge at Milan and returns to England after a tumultuous 14-month reign at Manchester United, where he was sacked in January. Milan lost their opening Europa League fixture 2-0 at home to Benfica, before battering Salzburg 4-0 in Austria, with Alphadjo Cisse netting a stunning hat-trick.

Crystal Palace are also in the Europa League tonight and face an incredibly daunting away trip to Turkish side Besiktas. Pressure is firmly on manager Pierre Sage following the 5-0 humiliation against Brighton last weekend and a shaky start to the season. Palace lost 3-2 to Sage’s former employers Lyon in their previous Europa League outing, with a positive performance and result needed to restore the fans’ faith.

Both games kick-off at 20:00, with team news coming imminently.

#1334. The numbers suggest Chelsea are pushovers as they slide down the Premier League table... and club legend GUS POYET says it's time to prove they're up for a fight

Published: 07:38 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 11:44 EST, 10 November 2026

Morgan Rogers insisted it was no intentional drive-by. That he did not mean to knee Trai Hume in the head while the Sunderland defender was sitting up after a foul. Just an accident, honest.

The history shared between these two particular players opened the incident to interpretation.

Hume had folded Rogers like a deckchair in a 1-1 draw for Aston Villa last season. The challenge went viral. Sunderland shared it on their social media, glamourising it. Rogers responded at the time by saying: 'Great message to send out. Dangerous tackles getting highlight reels.'

At the Stadium of Light on Sunday, Hume was starting to sit up when Rogers caught him. Chelsea were losing 1-0, and frustrated. Their £117million arrival from Villa apologised immediately, so we will believe him when he says it was an innocent collision rather than retribution.

Nevertheless, Rogers does have an aggressive side to him. He squared up with Declan Rice at Arsenal, and James Tarkowski at Everton, and was signed in the summer partially for that passion.

Rogers has contested more duels than any other Chelsea player this season. He loses more than he wins, but is involved, for better or worse. He is Xabi Alonso's most-fouled footballer, while nobody has committed more fouls than this 6ft 2in England international.

Morgan Rogers (right) showed some fight during Chelsea's loss at Sunderland that appears to be lacking across the whole squad

If Rogers' team-mates showed the same mentality they may have avoided defeat on Sunday

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso needs his side to develop an aggressive streak

So when we ponder whether Alonso's Chelsea are pushovers, Rogers is arguably an exception. He is a hard nut surrounded by a soft shell, and that was a problem at Sunderland.

It was not only that Brian Brobbey bullied Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana. Regis Le Bris' side were all at it, a team of bouncers ready to rough up the lads planning to party. Cole Palmer and Co ended up getting tossed out of the Stadium of Light on their rears. Chelsea recorded 69 per cent possession - their highest of the Premier League season so far - but were second-best throughout.

Gus Poyet saw that. He played for Chelsea, managed Sunderland, and was an assistant to Dennis Wise at Leeds, who will be the next visitors to Stamford Bridge after this international break.

Daniel Farke's side have won more duels and aerial duels than any other Premier League team this season, which, given what we witnessed on Sunday, should be a concern for Alonso.

Poyet can predict what is coming. Chelsea-Leeds is already a fixture with a narrative attached. It never needs a second invitation to be talked up as 'dirty'. Alonso's side will need to show a willingness to compete if that awaits, more than they managed when travelling to Sunderland.

'Sunderland went to the game with that old-fashioned mentality,' the 58-year-old Uruguayan told Daily Mail Sport. 'Pressure from the fans, noise, tackling, "I'm gonna run over you". Chelsea went on to try to play. There was quite a big difference in that aggression. We see teams that are looking so much for an identity that they forget the process to win games.'

Poyet brought up Chelsea's 2-0 win at Everton last month. We told him how Alonso had admitted it was his favourite performance of the season, describing it as 'solid' and 'serious'.

'There you go,' said Poyet, who thinks before travelling to the Stadium of Light, it would have been worth showing Chelsea's players videos from that victory at the Hill Dickinson. It was a rare showing of seriousness from Alonso's side. Only David Moyes' Everton, with 83, have committed fewer fouls than Chelsea's 95 in the Premier League this season. While giving away free-kicks is hardly a cause for celebration, it is not the worst way of measuring whether you are there to push or be pushed.

Sunderland striker Brian Brobbey (left) bulled Chelsea's Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana (right)

'For me that was a proper old-fashioned game, being able to win like that,' Poyet said about Chelsea's win at Everton. 'Put the video on and say, "Play the same".

'Now I know what the other side are going to say after watching the Sunderland game. Leeds will be saying, 'Let's go'. Leeds are very solid, and very aggressive, so it can be that kind of game.

'More and more, through the years, I think from the pandemic to now, the difference between the teams is mental. Identity, positions, shapes, blah, blah, blah, but when they are right in here (in the head), it's big. Right now, Leeds, as a team, are a little ahead mentally.'

Alonso is a polite manager. Given the chance to have a pop at the refereeing at the Stadium of Light - how Chelsea were not awarded a penalty when Cole Palmer was sandwiched, but Sunderland were when Brobbey dropped down in front of Colwill - he declined. The Blues boss chose instead to decry his team's defending as substandard. Colwill was hooked at half-time, while there were two new summer signings in the back line in Marco Palestra and Pep Chavarria who need to get to grips with the Premier League, sooner rather than later.

Poyet's first appearance after signing for Chelsea in 1997 was in the Charity Shield. Roy Keane welcomed him to English football with a kick to the head - with a little less subtlety than Rogers' knee on Hume. It finished 1-1 before Manchester United won on penalties.

Ex-Chelsea midfielder Gus Poyet has warned them of the threat Leeds pose later this month

Poyet learned a harsh lesson in that match, and not only from Keane's high kick. 'I couldn't get in the pace of the game,' Poyet recalls. 'I was always late. Ruud (Gullit) at half-time told me, "Gus, you're not really in the front, not really at the back". I said, "I'm trying!" The game was too fast.'

In a weird way, an ACL injury suffered by Poyet helped. He used the recovery time to prepare for returning. 'I went to the stadium, I was watching, learning the language, listening to Dennis Wise in the dressing room, getting that mentality,' he said. 'Then when I came back, I knew everything.

'That was my mentality. Some players need time. Some adjust quickly. You need to use all the time. For example, use this game against Sunderland when you play against Leeds. You cannot say, 'We didn't expect it'. Expect it! It's going to be similar.'

Football fans have the chance to enjoy a special afternoon with England legend and former Everton midfielder Paul Gascoigne at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Saturday 5 December (2pm).

Widely regarded as one of the most naturally-gifted players of his generation, Gazza earned 57 England caps, scored 10 international goals and became a national hero with his performances at Italia ’90 and his unforgettable goal against Scotland at Euro ’96.

Now, more than 25 years after first pulling on the Royal Blue shirt, Gazza will share memories of his time at Everton, the dressing room characters and former teammates, and recall fascinating stories from his career on some of football’s biggest stages.

Expect plenty of laughs, behind-the-scenes stories and unforgettable football memories as Gazza reflects on the moments and the people that shaped his extraordinary career.

#1332. Toothbrush zaps bacteria with electricity that’s made when bristles move

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

The history of the manual toothbrush has been traced back to the tenth-century Tang Dynasty in China. Credit: Valentyna Yeltsova/Getty

Researchers at Peking University in Beijing have developed a toothbrush in which bacteria are destroyed not only by mechanical friction, but also through an electrical charge that is generated by brushing. The work was published in Science Advances on 4 November1.

Generating electricity through brushing is a “new twist on an old concept”, says Frank Scannapieco, a periodontist at the University at Buffalo in New York. It might reduce plaque more efficiently than do conventional manual toothbrushes, although more tests are needed to prove efficacy and safety, he says.

The researchers showed that the brush did not damage the surface of the teeth and was not toxic to human cells, but they did not look at long-term safety or cost.

Bristled toothbrushes — which humans have used in various forms since the tenth century ad — rely mainly on motion to manually disrupt plaque, the film of bacteria, saliva and food particles that forms around teeth.

The team made the bristles from polyvinylidene fluoride, a polymer that they stretched and heated to obtain a piezoelectric form — meaning that it generated a charge when deformed.

When used to scrub teeth, the bending bristles release charges that create highly reactive forms of oxygen in nearby saliva. These molecules damage the cell membranes of bacteria in the plaque, say the researchers. When the bristles relax, the material reabsorbs the charges.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03586-y

Lu, Y. et al. Sci. Adv. 12, eaeg5744 (2026).
